# Copilot Prompts for the `napkin` Skill

Use these prompts with the Copilot skill located at:

`/.github/skills/napkin/skill.md`

This skill opens a browser-based interactive whiteboard (napkin.html on your Desktop) where you can draw, sketch, and add sticky notes to think through ideas visually. When you're ready, you share the whiteboard back to Copilot and it responds conversationally — interpreting your sketches, reading your sticky notes, and building on your thinking.

---


## dotNetDave-Ready Napkin Prompt

```text
Use the napkin skill to open a whiteboard.

After I sketch my idea and share it back, respond with:
1. A plain-English description of what you see — layout, sketches, arrows, groupings, and sticky note text.
2. Your interpretation of what I am trying to design or plan.
3. Any gaps, inconsistencies, or missing steps you notice.
4. Concrete suggestions for what to add or change.
5. A question to confirm whether your interpretation is correct before going further.

Keep the tone collaborative — you are building on my thinking, not analyzing my input.
```
---

## Opening a Napkin

```text
Use the napkin skill to open a whiteboard. I want to sketch out an idea visually before I explain it in words.
```

```text
Let's napkin.
```

```text
Open a napkin — I want to think through this visually.
```

```text
Start a whiteboard so I can sketch my idea and share it back with you.
```

---

## Reading a Napkin You Have Drawn

```text
Check the napkin.
```

```text
Look at the napkin and tell me what you see. Describe the layout, the sketches, and the sticky notes, and tell me what you think I'm trying to work out.
```

```text
Read my napkin and give me your interpretation. I want to know if what I sketched makes sense as a plan.
```

```text
I've shared my napkin — what do you think of the idea I sketched out?
```

---

## Building on a Napkin

```text
Check the napkin and then suggest improvements or additions to the idea I've sketched. Frame your suggestions as building on what I've already drawn.
```

```text
Look at the napkin and help me identify any gaps in the flow or steps I may have missed.
```

```text
Read the napkin and tell me if the process I sketched makes logical sense. Point out anything that looks out of order or disconnected.
```

```text
Check the napkin and suggest what I should add next to make this idea more complete.
```

---

## Turning a Napkin into a Document

```text
Check the napkin and then turn what I sketched into a structured document — use the layout and sticky notes as the outline.
```

```text
Read the napkin and convert it into a bulleted action plan based on what I drew.
```

```text
Look at the napkin and create a markdown summary of the idea, preserving the groupings and flow I drew.
```

```text
Check the napkin and draft a short memo based on what I sketched. Keep it plain English — no jargon.
```

---

## Architecture and Design Diagrams

```text
Use the napkin skill to open a whiteboard. I want to sketch a rough system architecture diagram and then get your feedback on the design before I write any code.
```

```text
Check the napkin. I've sketched a component diagram — describe what you see and tell me whether the component relationships and data flows make sense for the problem I described.
```

```text
Read the napkin. I've drawn a rough class or module structure. Tell me if the relationships I've drawn look correct and whether anything is missing.
```

```text
Look at the napkin. I've sketched a database schema or data model. Tell me if the entities and relationships I drew are reasonable and flag anything that looks like a design issue.
```

---

## Workflow and Process Sketches

```text
Use the napkin skill to open a whiteboard so I can sketch a business process or workflow before describing it in words.
```

```text
Check the napkin. I've drawn a workflow — describe the stages I sketched, identify the decision points, and tell me if the flow is clear or if any steps seem ambiguous.
```

```text
Read the napkin. I've mapped out a user journey. Tell me if the steps make sense from the user's perspective and whether there are any gaps in the experience.
```

## Brainstorming and Ideation

```text
Use the napkin skill to open a whiteboard. I want to dump ideas as sticky notes and then have you help me organize and prioritize them.
```

```text
Check the napkin. I've added a bunch of sticky notes with ideas. Group them into themes, identify any that seem most important, and flag any that overlap or conflict.
```

```text
Read the napkin and tell me which of the ideas I sketched seem most promising and which ones might be worth setting aside.
```
